Primary sources, fetched from GitHub on 2026-11-19:

## HolyArrs/HolyArrs (https://github.com/HolyArrs/HolyArrs)
Description: One self-hosted app for your shows, movies and music.
Homepage: https://holyarrs.com
Language: Go; license: AGPL-3.0; created 2026-11-09; last push 2026-11-18
Latest release: 1.2.0 (2026-11-17)
README (start):
English · Español · Français · Italiano · 简体中文 · 한국어 · 日本語 · हिन्दी · العربية · Русский · More languages

  
    
    
  

  

  
  
  
  
  
  

  

> [!NOTE]
> **HolyArrs 1.2.0: a red dot shows what needs attention, and connection tests name the exact problem.** Plex labels for requested titles, names in your language, and over 30 fixes. Connect apps over MCP with keys you control. [See what's new](https://holyarrs.com/whats-new/)

> Every poster, trailer and score in your HolyArrs comes from a server I run and pay for myself, so it stays free for everyone. If HolyArrs made movie night a little better, a sponsor keeps the lights on for all of us 💛
>
> 

> [!TIP]
> Be with us!
>
> | | |
> |:--|:--|
> |  | Get help fast and hang out on [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/mthsvesKpC) |
> |  | Share ideas and vote on [r/HolyArrs](https://reddit.com/r/HolyArrs) |
> |  | Sneak peeks on [X](https://x.com/CoderLuii) |
> |  | More projects on [GitHub](https://github.com/CoderLuii) |

Six apps to watch a show. Now it's one.

HolyArrs is one self-hosted app for your shows, movies and music.Browse like a streaming app, ask for what you want, and it handles the rest.

About 16.1 MB to download · about 95 MiB of RAM idle on a fresh install · amd64, arm64, armv7The six apps it replaces download 685.0 MB together.

Quick start · Why · What it does · Moving from other apps · The manual · Help

  

## 🚀 Running in two minutes

Save this as `docker-compose.yml` in a new folder on a local disk:

```yaml
name: holyarrs
services:
  holyarrs:
    image: holyarrs/holyarrs:latest
    container_name: holyarrs
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
    volumes:
      - /your/local/path:/config
      - /path/to/movies:/movies #optional
      - /path/to/tv:/tv #optional
      - /path/to/music:/music #optional
      - /path/to/downloads:/downloads #optional
    ports:
      - 6262:6262
    restart: unless-stopped
```

```sh
docker compose up -d
```

Open `http://your-server:6262` and make the owner account. A short setup walks you through folders, a downloader and a Source.

No API keys to hunt down. No second container. Every setting is explained in [the manual](#manual) further down.

## 💡 Why I built it

A normal media server runs six apps: Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Bazarr, Prowlarr and Seerr.

That's six logins, six ports, six update cycles and six API keys to copy between them. When a show doesn't land, you check six places to find out why.

I wanted one app. One login, one port, one place to look.

So I built it.

| App | Download (amd64) | Idle RAM | Logins | Web ports |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sonarr | 83.8 MB | | 1 | 1 |
| Radarr | 86.7 MB | | 1 | 1 |
| Lidarr | 115.7 MB | | 1 | 1 |
| Prowlarr | 77.1 MB | | 1 | 1 |
| Bazarr | 149.2 MB | | 1 | 1 |
| Overseerr | 172.4 MB | | 1 | 1 |
| **Six together** | **685.0 MB** | | **6** | **6** |
| **HolyArrs** | **16.1 MB** | **~140 MiB** | **1** | **1 (6262)** |

About 43 times smaller. Compressed size as shown on Docker Hub, linuxserver.io images, amd64, measured 2026-11-13 (HolyArrs 1.1.3). Idle RAM measured 2026-11-08 with 10,000 titles and 55,000 movies and episodes.

## 🎬 Ask for a title, and it shows up in your library

Someone asks for a title. HolyArrs searches your Sources, picks the best release with your Pick rules, sends it to your downloader and files it in your library. Your media server hears about it when it lands.

| | |
|---|---|
| 🍿 **Explore** | Browse like a streaming app. Hover a title and the trailer plays. |
| 🙋 **Requests** | A whole show or one season. You approve, or let trusted people skip the queue. Plex and Pulsarr watchlists can become requests. |
| 🎯 **Pick rules** | You decide which release wins: size, quality, language. |
| 💬 **Subtitles** | In the languages you pick, found on subtitle sites and kept with the file. |
| 📅 **Calendar** | What's airing next for everything you follow. |
| 🔔 **Alerts** | Discord, email, Telegram, ntfy, Gotify, Pushover or a webhook. |
| 🚚 **Import your setup** | From Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Prowlarr, Bazarr, Seerr, Overseerr, qBittorrent and SABnzbd. Pick what comes over, undo it later. |
| 🔌 **Old-app API** | Seerr, Prowlarr, Bazarr, Unpackerr and Homepage keep working once you turn it on. |
| 🗝️ **No API keys needed** | Titles, artwork and charts come from the HolyArrs metadata server. Your own keys or server work too. |
| 🔒 **Encrypted keys** | Stored passwords and keys are locked with a master key that lives in your config folder. |
| 🪶 **Tiny** | An image of about 16.1 MB with nothing but HolyArrs inside. |

See every page in motion

Home · Everything waiting on you, at a glance.
Title page · Trailer, cast and one button to ask.

Requests · Approve what friends and family ask for.
Downloads · Every grab, live, in one table.

## 🤝 It works with what you already run

- **Downloaders:** qBittorrent, Transmission, Deluge, rTorrent, aria2, SABnzbd, NZBGet
- **Media servers:** Plex, Jellyfin, Emby
- **Sources:** any Torznab or Newznab indexer, or Prowlarr or Jackett
- **Imports your setup from:** Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Prowlarr, Bazarr, Seerr, Overseerr, qBittorrent, SABnzbd

## 🚚 Bring your old setup with you

Open **Settings > Import from other apps**, add each old app's address and API key (or a backup zip), pick what comes over, then select **Import**. You can undo an import later.

| From | What comes over |
|---|---|
| Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr | Library folders, titles, quality profiles as Pick rules, exclusions, naming, indexers and download clients |
| Prowlarr | Indexers as Sources |
| Bazarr | Default subtitle languages |
| Seerr, Overseerr | People and their waiting or approved requests |
| qBittorrent, SABnzbd | Downloaders |

HolyArrs only reads your old apps and changes nothing in them, so you can run both side by side until you trust it.

Keys and passwords stay behind; you type them in again or import them from a file. Custom formats, tags and history don't come over. Media files never move. Step by step: [Import from other apps](https://docs.HolyArrs.com/migrate/).

## 🧭 What it doesn't do yet

- **Downloading by itself.** HolyArrs connects to qBittorrent, SABnzbd and the others. It doesn't replace them.
- **Phone and TV apps.** Not built. The web app works on a phone.
- **Music in Explore** is still being built.

What's next is on the [roadmap](https://holyarrs.com/roadmap/). You vote, I build. Post ideas on [r/HolyArrs](https://reddit.com/r/HolyArrs).

## ❓ Questions people ask first

**Do I keep qBittorrent or SABnzbd?**
Yes, for now. HolyArrs connects to the downloader you already run. A built-in downloader is planned for a later release.

**Can Sonarr and Radarr keep running while I try it?**
Yes. HolyArrs reads them once and never changes them.

**Is it free?**
Yes. It's free and open source.

---

# 📖 The manual

Everything below is reference. The full guides live at [docs.HolyArrs.com](https://docs.HolyArrs.com).

## Supported architectures

Pulling `holyarrs/holyarrs:latest` gets the right image for your machine.

| Architecture | Available | Runs on |
| :----: | :----: | --- |
| amd64 | ✅ | Most PCs, servers and NAS boxes |
| arm64 | ✅ | Apple silicon, newer Raspberry Pis, ARM servers |
| armv7 | ✅ | Older 32-bit ARM boards |

On a NAS? See [Unraid, Synology and other NAS boxes](https://docs.HolyArrs.com/run/platforms/).

Prefer a native package? An experimental Synology package (`.spk`) is attached to each [release](https://github.com/HolyArrs/HolyArrs/releases). See [Synology package](docs/run/synology.md).

## Version tags

Images live on Docker Hub as [`holyarrs/holyarrs`](https://hub.docker.com/r/holyarrs/holyarrs).

| Tag | Use it for |
| :----: | --- |
| `latest` | The newest release. |
| `1.1.4` | One exact version. It never moves. |

## Usage

### docker compose (recommended)

```yaml
name: holyarrs
services:
  holyarrs:
    image: holyarrs/holyarrs:latest
    container_name: holyarrs
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
    volumes:
      - /your/local/path:/config
      - /path/to/movies:/movies #optional
      - /path/to/tv:/tv #optional
      - /path/to/music:/music #optional
      - /path/to/downloads:/downloads #optional
    ports:
      - 6262:6262
    restart: unless-stopped
```

### docker cli

```sh
docker run -d \
  --name=holyarrs \
  -e PUID=1000 \
  -e PGID=1000 \
  -e TZ=America/New_York \
  -p 6262:6262 \
  -v /your/local/path:/config \
  -v /path/to/movies:/movies `#optional` \
  -v /path/to/tv:/tv `#optional` \
  -v /path/to/music:/music `#optional` \
  -v /path/to/downloads:/downloads `#optional` \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  holyarrs/holyarrs:latest
```

Container settings go in compose. Everything else is set in the app.

## Parameters

Each one is written `:`. Change the left side only.

| Parameter | Function |
| :----: | --- |
| `-p 6262:6262` | The web app. |
| `-e PUID=1000` | The user HolyArrs runs as. See [User and group](#user-and-group). |
| `-e PGID=1000` | The group HolyArrs runs as. |
| `-e TZ=America/New_York` | Your time zone, for the calendar, schedules and logs. `Etc/UTC` when left out. |
| `-e UMASK=022` | Optional. Permission bits new files leave out. Use `002` when a group must write too. |
| `-v /config` | Databases, settings, the master key, backups and logs. Local disk only, never a network share. |
| `-v /movies` | Optional. A movie Library folder. |
| `-v /tv` | Optional. A shows Library folder. |
| `-v /music` | Optional. A music Library folder. |
| `-v /downloads` | Optional. Your downloader's download folder. |
| `--read-only=true` | Optional. Only `/config` and `/tmp` need to be writable. |
| `--user=1000:1000` | Optional. Start as a fixed user. `PUID` and `PGID` are then ignored. |

More variables (reverse proxy, URL base, save path): [Environment variables](https://docs.HolyArrs.com/reference/env-vars/).

### Environment variables from files

Put `FILE__` in front of any variable to read its value from a file, such as a Docker secret:

```yaml
environment:
  - FILE__HOLYARRS_ALLOWED_HOSTS=/run/secrets/holyarrs_hosts
```

## User and group

`PUID` and `PGID` must match the user that owns your media folders. Find them with:

```sh
id youruser
# uid=1000(youruser) gid=1000(youruser)
```

HolyArrs never changes the owner of your media or download folders. Give that user write access to them, because HolyArrs makes folders and moves files.

## Application setup

Open `http://your-server:6262` and make the owner account right away. There is no default password. Until you make it, whoever opens HolyArrs first becomes the owner.

The setup that opens next asks for your folders, a downloader and a Source. Guide: [First run](https://docs.HolyArrs.com/start/first-run/).

### Media folders

The four optional mounts are the easy way to start. The cost: each mount is its own filesystem inside the container, so every import is a full copy.

Want instant moves that take no extra space? Mount one parent folder with downloads and Library folders inside it, and give your downloader the same mount at the same path. Guide: [Folders](https://docs.HolyArrs.com/start/folders/).

### Docker Desktop on Windows and Mac

Use a named volume for `/config`. Media folders can stay host folders. Guide: [Install](https://docs.HolyArrs.com/start/install/).

## Keep your master key safe

## Jellyfin Server

This repository contains the code for Jellyfin's backend server. Note that this is only one of many projects under the Jellyfin GitHub [organization](https://github.com/jellyfin/) on GitHub. If you want to contribute, you can start by checking out our [documentation](https://jellyfin.org/docs/general/contributing/index.html) to see what to work on.

## Server Development

These instructions will help you get set up with a local development environment in order to contribute to this repository. Before you start, please be sure to completely read our [guidelines on development contributions](https://jellyfin.org/docs/general/contributing/development.html). Note that this project is supported on all major operating systems except FreeBSD, which is still incompatible.

### Prerequisites

Before the project can be built, you must first install the [.NET 10 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet) on your system.

Instructions to run this project from the command line are included here, but you will also need to install an IDE if you want to debug the server while it is running. Any IDE that supports .NET 6 development will work, but two options are recent versions of [Visual Studio](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/) (at least 2022) and [Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/Download).

[ffmpeg](https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin-ffmpeg) will also need to be installed.

### Cloning the Repository

After dependencies have been installed you will need to clone a local copy of this repository. If you just want to run the server from source you can clone this repository directly, but if you are intending to contribute code changes to the project, you should [set up your own fork](https://jellyfin.org/docs/general/contributing/development.html#set-up-your-copy-of-the-repo) of the repository. The following example shows how you can clone the repository directly over HTTPS.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin.git
```

### Installing the Web Client

The server is configured to host the static files required for the [web client](https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin-web) in addition to serving the backend by default. Before you can run the server, you will need to get a copy of the web client since they are not included in this repository directly.

Note that it is recommended for development to [host the web client separately](#hosting-the-web-client-separately) from the web server with some additional configuration, in which case you can skip this step.

There are two options to get the files for the web client.

1. Build them from source following the instructions on the [jellyfin-web repository](https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin-web)
2. Get the pre-built files from an existing installation of the server. For example, with a Windows server installation the client files are located at `C:\Program Files\Jellyfin\Server\jellyfin-web`

### Running The Server

The following instructions will help you get the project up and running via the command line, or your preferred IDE.

#### Running With Visual Studio

To run the project with Visual Studio you can open the solution (`.slnx`) file and then press `F5` to run the server.

#### Running With Visual Studio Code

To run the project with Visual Studio Code you will first need to open the repository directory with Visual Studio Code using the `Open Folder...` option.

Second, you need to [install the recommended extensions for the workspace](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editor/extension-gallery#_recommended-extensions). Note that extension recommendations are classified as either "Workspace Recommendations" or "Other Recommendations", but only the "Workspace Recommendations" are required.

After the required extensions are installed, you can run the server by pressing `F5`.

#### Running From the Command Line

To run the server from the command line you can use the `dotnet run` command. The example below shows how to do this if you have cloned the repository into a directory named `jellyfin` (the default directory name) and should work on all operating systems.

```bash
cd jellyfin                          # Move into the repository directory
dotnet run --project Jellyfin.Server --webdir /absolute/path/to/jellyfin-web/dist # Run the server startup project
```

A second option is to build the project and then run the resulting executable file directly. When running the executable directly you can easily add command line options. Add the `--help` flag to list details on all the supported command line options.

1. Build the project

```bash
dotnet build                       # Build the project
cd Jellyfin.Server/bin/Debug/net10.0 # Change into the build output directory
```

2. Execute the build output. On Linux, Mac, etc. use `./jellyfin` and on Windows use `jellyfin.exe`.

#### Accessing the Hosted Web Client

If the Server is configured to host the Web Client, and the Server is running, the Web Client can be accessed at `http://localhost:8096` by default.

API documentation can be viewed at `http://localhost:8096/api-docs/swagger/index.html`

### Running from GitHub Codespaces

As Jellyfin will run on a container on a GitHub hosted server, JF needs to handle some things differently.

**NOTE:** Depending on the selected configuration (if you just click 'create codespace' it will create a default configuration one) it might take 20-30 seconds to load all extensions and prepare the environment while VS Code is already open. Just give it some time and wait until you see `Downloading .NET version(s) 7.0.15~x64 ...... Done!` in the output tab.

**NOTE:** If you want to access the JF instance from outside, like with a WebClient on another PC, remember to set the "ports" in the lower VS Code window to public.

**NOTE:** When first opening the server instance with any WebUI, you will be sent to the login instead of the setup page. Refresh the login page once and you should be redirected to the Setup.

There are two configurations for you to choose from.
#### Default - Development Jellyfin Server
This creates a container that has everything to run and debug the Jellyfin Media server but does not setup anything else. Each time you create a new container you have to run through the whole setup again. There is also no ffmpeg, webclient or media preloaded. Use the `.NET Launch (nowebclient)` launch config to start the server.

> Keep in mind that as this has no web client you have to connect to it via an external client. This can be just another codespace container running the WebUI. vuejs does not work from the get-go as it does not support the setup steps.

#### Development Jellyfin Server ffmpeg
this extends the default server with a default installation of ffmpeg6 though the means described here: https://jellyfin.org/docs/general/installation/linux#repository-manual
If you want to install a specific ffmpeg version, follow the comments embedded in the `.devcontainer/Dev - Server Ffmpeg/install.ffmpeg.sh` file.

Use the `ghcs .NET Launch (nowebclient, ffmpeg)` launch config to run with the jellyfin-ffmpeg enabled.

### Running The Tests

This repository also includes unit tests that are used to validate functionality as part of a CI pipeline on Azure. There are several ways to run these tests.

1. Run tests from the command line using `dotnet test`
2. Run tests in Visual Studio using the [Test Explorer](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/test/run-unit-tests-with-test-explorer)
3. Run individual tests in Visual Studio Code using the associated [CodeLens annotation](https://github.com/OmniSharp/omnisharp-vscode/wiki/How-to-run-and-debug-unit-tests)

### Advanced Configuration

The following sections describe some more advanced scenarios for running the server from source that build upon the standard instructions above.

#### Hosting The Web Client Separately

It is not necessary to host the frontend web client as part of the backend server. Hosting these two components separately may be useful for frontend developers who would prefer to host the client in a separate webpack development server for a tighter development loop. See the [jellyfin-web](https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin-web#getting-started) repo for instructions on how to do this.

To instruct the server not to host the web content, there is a `nowebclient` configuration flag that must be set. This can be specified using the command line
switch `--nowebclient` or the environment variable `JELLYFIN_HOSTWEBCLIENT=false`.

Since this is a common scenario, there is also a separate launch profile defined for Visual Studio called `Jellyfin.Server (nowebcontent)` that can be selected from the 'Start Debugging' dropdown in the main toolbar.

**NOTE:** The setup wizard cannot be run if the web client is hosted separately.

# The Application

### Settings

When you first run the application, you will be redirected to the settings page. Here you enter your desired upload directory for the video files, your [theMovieDb.org API key](https://www.themoviedb.org/documentation/api) and a different base URL if so desired (useful for remote hosting).

Once you made adjustments to any of the settings, make sure to validate the value before saving.
- For the API-Key, the validation checks against theMovieDb.org to see if you've entered a valid API-key.
- For the upload directory, the application checks if it has read/write permissions for it.

### The Dashboard

On the dashboard, a user can see their recently watched TV-shows and Movies and their progress (they can continue where they left off) as well start new shows and movies that they haven't yet seen. The "Continue Watching" Feature works by periodically updating the database (only while watching, of course!) with info about the currently watched Video and how far it has been seen.

If a Movie or Episode does not contain any video-files, it won't show up in the dashboard.

### The Player

The Streama-Player is (heavily) inspired by Netflix, so you get all the good stuff from there. For Shows, there is a "next episode" button and a handy episode/season browser. There are also the basics: volume-control, play/pause, and fullscreen. 
Later down the road I will add a feature to add subtitles and switch between video-files (for instance for different quality uploads). 
The player is HTML5-based and has only really been tested in Chrome so far.

##### The Episode Browser
I am especially proud of the Episode-Browser, which aims to function just like on Netflix. By default, the current video files season is selected. The user gets an overview of which other episodes there are in the season, how many seasons there are, and, as an added feature, the user sees all the added episodes, even if no video-files are added to them (thus greyed out).

### The Admin-Panel

One of the most important things to me was to make managing shows, movies, and episodes as easy and fun as possible. For this, I made heavy use of the API from [theMovieDatabase.org](https://www.themoviedb.org/), which auto-fills the episodes, shows and movies with useful information and great images. This eases the user's role in adding content.

For example, creating a new TV-show and the episodes for the first season looks something like this:

Uploading video-files for each episode is as easy as drag-and-drop!

  

### Accessing existing files
If you want to avoid uploading every file, use our new and improved "Local File" Feature instead. You can define a local directory (I use one directly in which I created symlinks to all my mounted drives) and then you can either use the local file browser for individual movies / tv-Shows or you can use the bulk-create feature.

HOLYARRS_FORWARD_AUTH_TRUSTED_PEERS	Proxy addresses or ranges allowed to send identity headers, comma separated.	none
HOLYARRS_FORWARD_AUTH_ALLOW_JOIN	New proxy names join as members who can only ask.	false

A bad setup stops HolyArrs from starting. Steps are in Sign-in and passwords.

Proxy variables
Link to Proxy variables

HolyArrs ignores HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY, in capitals or lowercase, on purpose. Before every outside connection, HolyArrs checks the real address it is about to reach, so that a lookup can never be steered to your local network. A proxy from the environment would connect for HolyArrs, to an address HolyArrs never sees, and that check would mean nothing.

When one of them is set, the log says so at start and the doctor shows a warning under Network. Posters, metadata and update checks still connect directly, and fail where your network blocks them. There is no app-wide proxy setting.

What to do instead:

Let HolyArrs reach the addresses in Outside addresses through your firewall.
For a Source that needs another route, set Proxy on that Source. It takes an HTTP or SOCKS5 proxy. See Sources.

## Folders | HolyArrs Docs
URL: https://docs.holyarrs.com/start/folders/
Description: Lay out one shared data folder so HolyArrs moves finished downloads into your Library instantly with hardlinks.

Skip to content
HolyArrs
On this page
Top of page
Folders

NEW HERE

Set up your folders once so finished downloads land in your Library instantly, without a second copy.

The Install example already mounts one data folder at /data. This page shows the layout inside it and how to give your downloader the same view. Mounting /movies, /tv, /music and /downloads one by one also works, but then every import is a full copy.

Already running with separate mounts? See Move to one data folder.

The rule
Link to The rule

Put downloads and media under one parent folder, on one disk, and mount that parent into HolyArrs and your downloader at the same path.

A hardlink is a second name for the same file. It takes no extra space and is made instantly. It only works inside one filesystem, and Docker treats every mount as its own, so separate mounts force a full copy.

/srv/data                  mounted as /data in HolyArrs and the downloader
├── downloads
│   ├── torrents
│   └── usenet
└── media
    ├── movies
    ├── tv
    └── music
Set it up
Link to Set it up

Make the folders on the host:

Terminal window
mkdir -p /srv/data/downloads/{torrents,usenet} /srv/data/media/{movies,tv,music}

Give your PUID user write access:

Terminal window
chown -R 1000:1000 /srv/data

Mount the parent in HolyArrs: - /srv/data:/data.

Mount it the same way in your downloader: - /srv/data:/data, and set its save folder to /data/downloads/torrents or /data/downloads/usenet.

In HolyArrs, use /data/media/movies, /data/media/tv and /data/media/music as Library folders during First run.

You should see Instant, no extra space on each folder in Settings > Library folders.

CAUTION

Separate NAS shares or datasets under /srv/data are separate filesystems. Files still copy between them. Use folders inside one share.

Hardlink, move or copy
Link to Hardlink, move or copy

When a download finishes, HolyArrs puts each file in your Library in one of three ways:

DOWNLOAD	SAME MOUNT AND DISK	DIFFERENT MOUNTS OR DISKS
Torrent	Hardlink. The downloader keeps seeding the same file.	Copy. The torrent keeps its own file.
Usenet, or a file HolyArrs unpacked	Move.	Copy. HolyArrs then clears the finished job, with its files, from SABnzbd or NZBGet.
A hardlink or a move is instant and takes no extra space. A copy takes as long as writing the file again, and the file sits on disk twice until the downloader’s copy is gone.
Before a copy, HolyArrs checks there is room for the file. It writes the copy under a hidden .holyarrs- name in the target folder and gives it its real name only when it is complete, so a half-written file never shows in your Library.
A copy shows in History as by copy (hardlink not possible).
HolyArrs never moves files out of a downloader it may not change (HolyArrs can change this Downloader off, or HOLYARRS_READONLY_DOWNLOADERS), or out of a Library folder. Those files are hardlinked, or copied.
Choices
Link to Choices
Separate mounts
Link to Separate mounts

/movies, /tv, /music and /downloads as four mounts still work. Every import then copies the file, which takes longer and uses double the space until the downloader deletes its copy. That holds for Usenet downloads too, even on one disk: a file can only move instantly within one mount, so use the shared parent folder above.

Downloader in another container with other paths
Link to Downloader in another container with other paths

If the downloader sees the folder under another name, fill in Downloader’s path and HolyArrs’ path on the downloader in Settings > Downloaders, such as /data/torrents and /downloads. Matching paths need no mapping.

If it does not work
Link to If it does not work
YOU SEE	CAUSE	FIX
Each import makes a full copy (uses extra space) on a Library folder	Downloads and media are on different mounts or filesystems	Mount one parent folder, as above. Already set up? See Move to one data folder
Cannot write here or Folder not found	The path is wrong, or PUID cannot write	Use the path inside the container; fix ownership
A folder is not found	You typed the host path	Type the container path, such as /data/media/movies
Import says the path is not allowed	The download folder is not a known place	Set HOLYARRS_SAVE_PATH, or add it under Settings > Library folders > Extra import folders
